qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Serves approximately one-third of Germany's Mittelstand corporate clients and 11M retail customers. However, operates in Germany's notoriously fragmented, structurally unprofitable banking market dominated by state-subsidized Sparkassen and non-profit cooperative banks (Volksbanken). Multi-cycle ROE has averaged just 2-5% (2018: 3.1%, 2019: 2.0%, 2020: -10.4%, 2021: 1.5%, 2022: 4.8%), completely failing the 12% capital efficiency hurdle. Lacks pricing power in commoditized corporate credit and deposit gathering.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC/ROE < 12%, REJECT). Second-largest private German lender heavily focused on corporate Mittelstand lending and retail banking. Structurally trapped in Germany's triple-pillar banking system where non-profit public and cooperative banks depress industry net interest margins. Multi-cycle ROE averaged 2-5% over 2018-2022 (peaking at ~7.8% in 2024), falling far short of the 12% hurdle. Lacks pricing power and faces takeover uncertainty from UniCredit.
qualitative.evidence: Historical ROE track record: 3.1% (2018), 2.0% (2019), -10.4% (2020), 1.5% (2021), 4.8% (2022), 7.0% (2023), 7.8% (2024). 7-year median ROE of ~3.1% is among the lowest of major European banks. Cost-to-income ratio historically exceeded 75-80%, reflecting high German labor/restructuring costs and inability to re-price commoditized corporate lending.
